title: The full pipeline on a real document through brain.reason, and a flan-t5-small vs Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct fidelity comparison
goal: Prove, end to end and through the single lab.common.brain.reason entry point (not a hand-assembled call sequence), that a real, previously-unseen document can be given as raw text plus an ask and come out the other side as a cited, consistency-checked, formatted .docx -- with dslim/bert-base-NER (EXP-080) actually live in the loop, not just standalone-measured -- and measure whether Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (permitted 2026-10-18, FORBIDDEN.md) improves the rewriter's fidelity pass rate on this same fixture over flan-t5-small's measured 0% (this exploration's own earlier run), testing the hypothesis that the failure is about training quality, not raw parameter count.
method: A real ~2,400-word, 13-article GDPR excerpt (fetched live from gdpr-info.eu, embedded here as a fixture for reproducibility) auto-chunked by lab.common.ingest.chunk_document into 69 passages, then passed with an ask to lab.common.brain.reason(use_real_ner=True) -- the real dispatch path, which always uses write_long_document's default checkpoint (flan-t5-small). Separately, the identical findings are run through two direct lab.common.longform.write_long_document calls, each naming a different checkpoint explicitly (flan-t5-small, then Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct), same fidelity gate, same findings, same use_real_ner=True -- a controlled before/after on the one variable that changed.

ask_tried_first.text: Rewrite this regulation into a clear, well-organized compliance summary.

ask_that_fires.text: Write a document summarizing this regulation in plain language.

results_prose: Auto-chunked a real 2,368-word, 13-article GDPR excerpt into 69 passages with no manual pre-structuring. 'Rewrite this regulation into a clear, well-organized compliance summary.' (the phrasing tried by hand first) scores 0.6795 against wants_document's 0.75 threshold -- does NOT fire. 'Write a document summarizing this regulation in plain language.' scores 0.7846 -- fires. brain.reason (which always uses the default checkpoint, flan-t5-small) dispatched to lab.common.longform as expected and returned decision='supported_with_flags' with 69 citations. Checkpoint comparison on the identical 18-leaf fixture: flan-t5-small passed the fidelity gate on 0/18 leaves (0.0), Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct on 0/18 (0.0) -- Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct did NOT improve the fidelity pass rate on this real document. flan-t5-small's dominant failure reasons: ['deterministic_splice_preferred', 'already_complete']; Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct's: ['deterministic_splice_preferred', 'already_complete']. Both checkpoints' .docx/.md files were written to disk for direct comparison.
conclusion: Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct did NOT measurably improve the fidelity pass rate over flan-t5-small on this real document -- see metrics.rewrite_fidelity_by_checkpoint for the exact failure reasons each checkpoint hit. This is evidence that dense modal/numeric regulatory language defeats the fidelity gate's current thresholds somewhat independent of which small checkpoint generates the rewrite, not just a flan-t5-small-specific weakness. Reported as measured, not assumed to improve just because a newer or larger model was substituted. brain.reason itself still defaults to flan-t5-small (write_long_document's own default checkpoint) -- this comparison used direct write_long_document calls with each checkpoint named explicitly; making Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct the live default for brain.reason's own dispatch is a separate decision, not made here.
scale_down: One real document (69 passages, 19 leaves), two checkpoints -- a genuine end-to-end proof and a real controlled comparison, not a benchmark across many documents, domains, or checkpoints.
follow_ups: If Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct's fidelity pass rate is still well under 1.0, the next checkpoints to try on this identical fixture are the already-registered nagbhaskar55/gemma-3-270m-bhaskar-finetune (EXP-076) and gemma3:270m, to separate 'needs a bigger/different base model' from 'needs domain-specific fine-tuning' as the actual fix.

wants_document's threshold (tau=0.75) is phrasing-sensitive enough that a natural first attempt ('rewrite this regulation...') fails to fire it -- worth either lowering tau with a wider calibration set (EXP-079 only calibrated against 3 document asks and 4 lookup asks) or accepting the current precision/recall tradeoff explicitly rather than by accident.

brain.reason's longform dispatch still hardcodes flan-t5-small as write_long_document's default checkpoint -- making the better-measured checkpoint the live default (rather than only reachable via a direct write_long_document call) is a separate, deliberate decision, not made in this exploration.

The cross-page consistency checker's false-positive rate on repetitive legal text (same generic subject, many unrelated clauses) was not measured here, only observed qualitatively -- a dedicated precision measurement is a real follow-up before trusting this flag on this kind of document.
models_used: dslim/bert-base-NER (entity detection, live via use_real_ner=True, not generative) + flan-t5-small and Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (bounded rewriter role, fidelity-gated, each run on the identical 19-leaf fixture for a controlled comparison) via lab.common.rewriter_backends.
